answer_1.quote: Multi-document summarization (MDS) aims to formulate a summary that captures the essence and main points of multiple documents on a specific topic.

answer_2.quote: We benchmark our study on the quantitative metrics -Rouge-1 (R1), Rouge-2 (R2) and Rouge-L (RL) , to evaluate the lexical overlap, as well as on qualitative metrics -BARTScore to compute the semantic overlap, and FactCC , and SummaC for faithfulness assessment.

answer_3.quote: We also employed the BARTScore , and SummaC  metrics to evaluate the semantic overlap and faithfulness between the system-generated summaries and the reference summaries.

answer_4.quote: We conducted a human evaluation to assess the qualitative aspects of the summaries generated by FABRIC. The evaluation focused on five parameters -Informativeness (Inf), Relevance (Rel), Coherence (Coh), Fluency (Flu), and Topic coherence (Topic). ... we randomly selected 50 test samples ... engaged 30 annotators ... each sample was annotated by at least two annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated each summary on Informativeness, Relevance, Coherence, Fluency, and Topic Coherence.
